stage1.impression: A clean, legible range shot with a good idea: eight tinted acrylic speakers backlit low so each throws a coloured pool of light forward on pale paper. But it reads as a tidy CG catalogue render rather than a photograph: the paper is a dead-flat, textureless white, most of each cast shadow is a heavy neutral grey with the colour only at the tip, the cabinet faces are dim and murky with crushed woofers, the smoked unit is a near-black hole, and the even rainbow line-up feels toy-like rather than $20,000.

blocking_9: Paper must read as real paper: visible tooth and a gentle light falloff toward the bottom of the frame instead of a flat 237 field (range 2)
The cast light must be the story: coloured light should dominate each throw, with the neutral batt shadows lifted so they no longer read as heavy grey slabs (now median 107 against paper 237)
Cabinet faces must read as lit tinted acrylic with readable woofers, not murky dark fronts (red face median 80, woofers median 11)
The smoked speaker must read as smoked acrylic with visible interior and edges, not a black cut-out (body median 16, 3.4 % crushed)
No bright cove band at the horizon; wall and floor must share one white balance
Camera and arrangement must feel art-directed and monumental, not a toy row seen from above

defects.what: Foreground paper dead flat (lum 236-238, range 2): no tooth, no falloff; reads as a CG plane
Wall flat and warm grey (214,211,210) while the lit floor is cool (237,237,240): two white balances in one set
Bright cove band at the horizon (median 221, p95 241) brighter than the wall above it: visible seam between wall and floor
Batt shadows are heavy neutral grey slabs (median 107) that dominate each throw; coloured light only appears as a small patch at the far tip
Smoked speaker crushed to near black (median 16), interior and edges unreadable; its shadow has no colour at all
Front faces in shade and murky (red median 80); woofer cones crushed (median 11)
Red and orange throws overlap and tangle with the back-rank shadow; busy and confusing at the left
Horns read as separate objects floating on thin rods above the cabinets, with a dark blob of driver inside each
Clear speaker's white ring and grey batts read as flat card and plastic, with little refraction or edge light in the acrylic
Even, repeated rainbow line-up seen from slightly above reads as a toy or catalogue grid rather than a hero

changes.problem: The neutral batt shadows are heavy grey slabs that overpower the coloured light, so the image reads as grey shadows with coloured tips rather than colour passing through acrylic.

evidence.measured: shadow median 107, RGB 111/106/94, against open paper 237; coloured patch (yellow) 360-500 x 520-545 median 209

change.setting: over (silk over the floor in front of the line)

changes.expected: Grey shadow cores lift to about 140-155 so they read as soft shade, while the sun-cast coloured pools keep their saturation and become the dominant shape on the floor.

changes.problem: The cabinet fronts sit in murky shade and the woofers are crushed, so the hero surfaces do not read.

evidence.measured: red face median 80, p5 45; woofer cone 300-380 x 300-340 median 11

change.setting: face (softbox light-linked to cabinets, linings, rings) and strip (woofers)

changes.expected: Faces glow as lit tinted acrylic (red face median about 105-125), the coloured rings read, and the cones show a soft gradient instead of a black disc.

changes.problem: The paper is a dead-flat, textureless plane that says render.

changes.expected: Fine paper grain is visible in the foreground at full size, with a few levels of variation instead of 2.

changes.problem: The smoked speaker is a black cut-out with no readable acrylic.

change.setting: smoke (strip light-linked to the smoked speaker)
change.to: 45 W/m2, moved to (3.5, 1.0, 1.6) so it rims the near edge and passes through the side panel

changes.expected: The smoked cabinet reads as dark tinted glass: lit edges, visible ribs and batts behind it, body median about 30-45.

changes.problem: The cove shows as a brighter band at the horizon, a seam between wall and floor.

evidence.measured: median 221, p95 241 against the wall above at 211

change.from: top 7.0 W/m2; cyc 13.0 W/m2 centred 1.5 m up

changes.expected: The wall grades smoothly into the floor with no band; the horizon zone matches the wall within a few levels.

changes.problem: The wall is warm grey while the lit floor is cool white, so the set reads as two worlds.
changes.expected: Floor reads as warm paper close to #EEECE7 (blue no higher than red), consistent with the wall.

changes.problem: The throws of the front and back ranks tangle at the left, muddying the colour story.

change.from: back rank 1.2 m behind, centres 0.64 m apart

changes.expected: Eight separate coloured lanes on the floor, each clearly attributable to its speaker.

changes.problem: Seen from 1.7 m with a 50 mm lens, the row reads as a toy line-up from above rather than monumental 1.3 m loudspeakers.

evidence.measured: the horizon sits at about y 250, above the horns' bases; the cabinet tops are seen from above

change.to: (0, -12.5, 1.15), 70 mm, f/4 focused on the front rank, reframed so the title still has the top fifth clear

changes.expected: Speakers read at eye height with presence, the ranks compress into one gesture, and both ranks hold focus.

out_of_scope.request: Close the visual gap between horn and cabinet, or make the rods read as a deliberate bracket
out_of_scope.why: The horns read as floating separate objects, but the horn mount is part of the speaker's fixed design

out_of_scope.request: Make the compression driver inside the horn less of a black blob
out_of_scope.why: It is a fixed part of the speaker; only light (the strip already reaches it) may change

out_of_scope.request: Make the white batts read less like grey card through the clear and tinted acrylic
out_of_scope.why: The batts are a fixed part of the speaker's construction
